overview: 62 new pieces in the last 48 hours across 12 sources. Most of it is about software engineering, AI tools, AI research.

reads.title: [AINews] Riemann Hypothesis proved...twice independently
reads.author: swyx .ai
reads.summary: Within a few hours of each other ( timeline ), two mathematicians claimed independent proofs of the Riemann Hypothesis, the most famous open problem in mathematics ( Scientific American ). Levent Alpöge of Anthropic first made his Claude-driven proof in a note released with Lean code (1.3GB worth, ~250,000 page equivalent) rather than a full paper.

reads.title: The War Against Slop and an Emerging Weapon to Fight it: Formal Verification
reads.author: Richard MacManus
reads.description: Proving software correct with math has traditionally required specialist work. Now AI and Lean are helping automate the process.
reads.summary: The word of the year in the AI industry over 2026 has been “slop” — meaning low-quality output from a large language model. And with so much code being AI-generated now, avoiding slop has become a daily concern for software engineers.

reads.title: Fragments: November 20
reads.author: Martin Fowler (martin@martinfowler.com)
reads.description: Marcus Borg recounts an experiment to investigate if healthy code was cheaper for agents to review . Between a typical unhealthy pull request (CodeHealth 2.8) and a typical healthy one (9.7), that adds up to 22 to 35%. The measures of health come from CodeScene. The experiment looked at three LLMs, 465 pull requests…

reads.title: Gemini 4 Neon Draws a Python Reading a Book

reads.title: Anthropic announces closing of initial public offering, including full exercise of underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares, and closing of concurrent private placement
reads.author: Anthropic
reads.description: Today Anthropic, PBC announced the closing of its initial public offering of an aggregate of 1,127,000,000 shares of its Class A common stock at a public offering price of $83.00 per share, including the full exercise by the underwriters of their option to purchase an additional 147,000,000 shares of Class A common…
reads.summary: The offering consisted of 1,103,351,354 shares sold by Anthropic and 23,648,646 shares sold by certain selling stockholders. The aggregate gross proceeds from the offering, before deducting underwriting discounts and commissions and other offering expenses, were approximately $93.5 billion, of which approximately $91.6 billion was received by Anthropic.
